title: Dynamic BH3 profiling method for rapid identification of active therapy in BH3 mimetics resistant xenograft mouse models
protocol: Obtain human leukemia cells from a bone marrow biopsy.
Subject bone marrow aspirate (BMA) of a human patient to Ficoll-Paque gradient to isolate mononuclear cells.
Dilute the BMA 1:5 with PBS at 20°C–22°C.
Filter diluted BMA through a 70 μm cell strainer into a Falcon tube.
Layer filtered BMA onto the Ficoll-Paque gradient.
Centrifuge at 400 × g for 30 minutes at 20°C–22°C without the brake.
Collect the white blood cells from the interphase layer and transfer to a new 50 mL Falcon tube.
Add 4°C PBS to achieve a final volume of 50 mL and mix by inversion.
Centrifuge at 600 × g for 5 minutes at 20°C–22°C.
Look for pellet; aspirate the supernatant.
Resuspend the cells in 5 mL of 4°C PBS to a final volume of 30 mL.
Count the cells.
Centrifuge at 600 × g for 5 minutes at 20°C–22°C.
Look for pellet; aspirate the supernatant.
Resuspend mononuclear cells in 200 μL of 20°C–22°C PBS.
Place the mice under a lamp light to warm them and make tail veins visible.
Sterilize the mouse’s tail with an alcohol wipe.
Inject 0.6–1.0 × 10^6 human leukemia cells in 200 μL of PBS intravenously (IV).
Bleed mice weekly to evaluate circulating peripheral blast counts and engraftment progress via flow cytometry.
Using a surgical lancet, puncture the facial submandibular vein and collect 20–50 μL of blood in a microtainer blood collection tube.
Lyse the cells by adding a 1:10 ratio of blood:RBC lysis buffer (Qiagen).
Incubate for 10 minutes in a 5 mL FACS tube at 20°C–22°C.
Wash the cells with 4 mL of PBS.
Incubate the sample with lysis buffer for no longer than 10 minutes to avoid unwanted cell population lysis.
Centrifuge the sample at 600 × g for 5 minutes at 20°C–22°C.
Aspirate the supernatant after centrifugation.
Resuspend the pellet in FACS staining buffer.
Stain the resuspended cells with hCD45 antibody diluted at a ratio of 1:100.
Perform FACS analysis to determine the percentage of human myeloblasts by gating on SSClowhCD45dim cells.
Sacrifice mice when FACS analysis reveals more than 70% circulating human myeloblasts.
Euthanize mice in a CO2 chamber with a delivery rate of 10%–30% of the chamber volume per minute.
Remove spleen and collect pelvis, femur, and tibia bones from both legs after exposing the peritoneum.
Proceed with tissue processing for serial passaging of leukemia cells.
Place spleen onto 70 μm cell strainer on top of a 50 mL Falcon tube.
Add 5 mL PBS, smash the spleen using the plunger from a 5 mL syringe.
Add 20 mL PBS to prepare a single cell suspension.
Crush all bones in 1 mL of PBS using a mortar and pestle.
Filter the bones through a 70 μm cell strainer on top of a 50 mL Falcon tube to prepare a single cell suspension.
Resuspend cells in RBC lysis buffer (Qiagen) for 5 min at 20°C–22°C.
Wash the cells with 4 mL of PBS.
Resuspend 0.6–1.0 × 10^6 spleen myeloblasts in 200 μL of PBS.
Begin continuous treatment of leukemia-bearing mice with BH3 mimetics until leukemia blasts relapse, indicating acquired drug resistance.
Bleed the mice weekly using section 1 steps 6 and 7 to assess for circulating peripheral blasts.
Begin treatment with BH3 mimetics when FACS analysis reveals >5% circulating peripheral blasts.
Use an oral gavage feeding tube to administer 100 mg/kg venetoclax, PO, 5 days per week.
Use a 281/2g needle to inject 40 mg/kg S6383845, IV, 2 days per week.
Continue to bleed the mice weekly to assess for circulating peripheral blasts.
Sacrifice the mice when FACS analysis reveals >70% circulating peripheral blasts.
Harvest bones and spleen following section 1 steps 8a-c after sacrifice.
Perform dynamic BH3 profiling on cells with acquired resistance to BH3 mimetics.
Seed myeloblasts harvested from the spleen and bone marrow in a 24-well plate at a density of 1.0 × 10^6 cells per mL of RPMI per well.
Treat with desired drug panel for 14–16 hours at 37°C.
Collect the cells for downstream processing in 1.5 mL Eppendorf tubes.
Centrifuge collected cells at 600 × g for 5 minutes at 20°C to 22°C.
Look for pellet and aspirate supernatant.
Resuspend 1.0 × 10^6 cells in 100 μL of FACS staining buffer.
Incubate with 1 μL Fc blocker in the dark at 4°C for 15 minutes.
Wash cells with 1 mL of PBS.
Prepare a cocktail of antibodies and Zombie Yellow Fixable Viability dye in 100 μL of FACS staining buffer, each at a 1:100 dilution.
Incubate stained cells in the dark at 4°C for 30 minutes.
Wash cells with 1 mL of PBS.
Proceed with downstream processing.
Thaw pre-made peptide plates in a 26°C incubator for at least 30 min before use.
Centrifuge PBS-washed cells at 600 × g for 5 min at 20°C–22°C.
Aspirate the supernatant from centrifuged cells.
Resuspend cells at 5 × 10^4 cells per 15 μL MEB buffer.
Transfer 15 μL cell suspension to a 384W BH3 peptide plate.
Mix cells with BH3 peptides by gently tapping all four sides of the plate.
Incubate cells with BH3 peptides in a 26°C incubator for 60 min.
Add 10 μL of 4% paraformaldehyde to each well to fix the cells and terminate BH3 peptide exposure.
Repeat mixing after adding formaldehyde, then incubate for 15 min at 20°C–22°C.
Add 10 μL of N2 buffer to each well to neutralize 4% paraformaldehyde and terminate cell fixation.
Incubate the cells with N2 buffer by repeating mixing and incubating for 10 min at 20°C–22°C.
Add 10 μL of pre-made CytoC staining buffer and antibody mixture to each well.
Repeat mixing after adding CytoC solution, then incubate overnight (14–16 h) at 4°C in the dark.
Mix well is very important to ensure homogenous staining across each well.
Cover the plate with an adhesive sealing film.
Shake the plate from side to side thoroughly.
Proceed with acquisition and FACS analysis.
